forecast_issue: End of previous calendar month. Key rate available through issue month. Bank rates through issue month minus release lag. Latest observed bank rate is the reference for the predicted change. Historical revisions are not reconstructed.
training: Single fit at first forecast issue per window. All real training and validation targets released by that issue. ARX and the existing small transformer use the same information timestamps. Transformer uses an earlier fitting subset and a trailing validation subset with nonoverlapping target information dates.
windows_status: B and E informed the hypotheses. F was not used in the previous forecast experiment, but dates overlap prior response diagnostics. B starts in March because calibration B requires December 2021 releases. Three-month release lag excludes March 2022 as well.
matched_paths: ABM, twin, partial and weak see the same synthetic key-rate paths by repetition. ABM and weak also share parameter draws and random seeds. Only the direct pricing coefficients differ between ABM and weak.
partial_adjustment: Per series, r[t] = (1-lambda)r[t-1] + lambda(a+b k[t]) + error, with 0.05 <= lambda <= 0.95 and 0 <= b <= 1.5. Fit on all available real rates since 2014-01 at first forecast issue. Simulate with joint residual resampling and equilibrium initialization at the first scenario key rate. The partial generator takes no simulated bank states from ABM.
simple_forecaster: Direct ridge ARX, own rate changes over 1, 3 and 6 months relative to latest release, key rate changes over 1, 3 and 6 months through issue, current key rate minus latest released bank rate. Real-train standardization, ridge 0.01. Naive persistence is scored separately.
direct_validation: Use calibration B in 2022-01 through 2026-09 with 24 months of historical warmup. Use the repository's same local projection on observations and simulated outputs under the observed monthly key-rate path. Also estimate a common-random-number step of +2 pp vs flat. Local projections describe associations for the observed policy path.
direct_hypothesis: ABM approximately reproduces the scale and timing of pass-through. Primary diagnostic is RMSE of the 16 LP coefficient differences, with four rates and four horizons. Compare with absolute beta <= 0.25 pp per pp as a descriptive margin per cell, and compare the original ABM with the variant halving direct pricing coefficients. Report estimated real confidence intervals separately from simulator seed variation.
forecast_hypotheses: ABM augmentation reduces RMSE relative to training on real observations alone. Compare ABM to twin and partial to assess compression and to weak to assess the contribution of the direct pricing rule. Also compare to persistence.
forecast_primary_summary: RMSE in percentage points, pooled per window and over all windows with equal weight per month and rate. Ratio below 0.95 denotes a point improvement of practical size, ratio above 1.05 a point deterioration. Values between thresholds are descriptive. An interval spanning the relevant margins leaves practical equivalence unresolved.
uncertainty: Paired circular moving-block bootstrap of forecast months drawn inside each window, all four rates together, blocks of 3 months, 2000 draws and central 90% interval. Report each paired repetition as well as the ensemble; block intervals condition on the realized windows and learned ensembles.
positive_control: A synthetic observable law with a fixed delayed linear key-rate component and selectable nonlinear positive/negative large-jump component. Test identical ARX pipeline on windows of the same lengths against a generator with the correct rule and a generator omitting nonlinearity. If needed to detect nonlinearity, use the same explicit absolute-jump feature on both sides. Check that the procedure can detect intentionally observable forecast information. This is a smoke test for statistical design and timing, not evidence about the real DGP.
limitations: Deposits in ABM are stock-weighted current bank quotes, while CBR rates use new operations. Rates represent different aggregates in this segment. Forecast usefulness, fit of observed pass-through, and causal policy effects are distinct. Only one model and few macro episodes are available. No current-vintage claim is made.
